prediction_ref.short_label: Anthropic-AWS pact locks 5-pole hyperscaler-lab regime by H1 2027

validation_rows.evidence_summary: [REVIVED] Layer-1 signal hit on Google-Gemini / platform-exclusive: today's WWDC keynote lands a major new bilateral device-maker-to-frontier-lab alliance squarely inside this thesis's domain. Apple rebuilt Siri on a custom roughly 1.2-trillion-parameter Google Gemini model under a multi-year deal reported around $1 billion a year, with analyst estimates of total value up to $5 billion. After years of failing to ship a competitive in-house assistant, the most vertically integrated device maker has paired off with a frontier lab for the brain of its flagship AI feature, layering a second multi-billion-dollar commercial tie on top of the existing default-search payment Google already makes Apple. This densifies the multi-pole model-alliance regime: the assistant tier is consolidating into named lab pairings rather than fragmenting. The caveat that keeps this from a 5 is mechanism - Apple is a device maker (not a hyperscaler) and the arrangement is a license to run a custom model behind Apple's own Private Cloud Compute topology, not the exclusive hardware-codesigned cloud pact (Trainium/TPU-class) the original 5-pole framing centered on; the alliance is real but the exclusivity-and-codesign leg is absent.

prediction_ref.short_label: Closed-weight frontier crystallizes as open weights cap at 35B-A3B by Q3 2026

validation_rows.evidence_summary: [REVIVED] Layer-2 semantic match on the proprietary-re-expansion / local-for-utility-cloud-for-frontier split. Apple, which had been building its own foundation models, concluded its in-house effort had fallen a generation behind - the licensed Gemini is described as about eight times larger than the biggest cloud model Apple had built in-house - and chose to rent a proprietary closed frontier model rather than keep training one. Apple's privacy-by-topology design instantiates the split the thesis names: a roughly 3-billion-parameter on-device model handles local utility requests, and heavier work routes to the closed frontier model under Private Cloud Compute with PII stripped before reaching the Gemini layer. That even a firm with Apple's resources renting-rather-than-building the frontier is a clean directional signal that the closed frontier is pulling away from what self-built models can match. Relevance is held at 3, not higher, because today's news is about a device maker outsourcing to a rival's closed model - it does not speak to the prediction's specific falsifiable mechanism, an open-weights ceiling crystallizing around the 35B-A3B class.

prediction_ref.short_label: On-device LLM silicon ships 1-PFLOP deskside + sandbox-runtime specs by H1 2027

validation_rows.evidence_summary: Layer-2 semantic match on the on-device-LLM-ecosystem leg, against a cohort member this prediction named explicitly. The June 1 thesis listed Apple M-series + Core ML / MLX heading into WWDC June 8 as a peer expected to publish deskside-class on-device LLM specs paired with an OS-sandbox runtime at agent-invocation granularity. WWDC delivered half of that pairing: the Foundation Models framework now exposes Apple's on-device model to developers for tool-calling and guided (structured) generation with no per-call charge, turning the device into an addressable on-device-LLM surface for developers. The sandbox-runtime-at-agent-invocation-granularity half is explicitly still open - the keynote left how strict the entitlements and tool-permission model will be to the detailed API sessions running June 9-12. So today advances the on-device-model-exposure side of the prediction but not yet the named-OS-sandbox-runtime side, and it is a consumer-class on-device model rather than the 1-PFLOP deskside-silicon floor the prediction quantifies. A genuine partial touch on the local-LLM ecosystem thesis, scored mid.

prediction_ref.short_label: Open agent harness powers a second vendor's first-party agent by Q4 2026

validation_rows.evidence_summary: Layer-2 semantic match on the agent-platform / agent-surface theme. WWDC opened the largest consumer device base as an addressable agent surface in two directions at once: deeper App Intents lets the new assistant chain multi-step tasks across third-party apps, and the Foundation Models framework lets those apps call a free on-device LLM for tool use and structured output. That is the same agent-harness-as-platform pattern this prediction tracks - the differentiated work moving to the governance, identity and product surface around a reusable agent loop. The important honest qualifier is that Apple is in part a counter-instance to the prediction's specific mechanism: it built its agent surface on its own first-party frameworks (App Intents plus Foundation Models) rather than embedding an open-source harness, so it does not itself confirm an open harness powering a second vendor's first-party agent. Where it leans toward the thesis is the model layer - the system assistant became a user-selectable slot (Siri, Gemini, ChatGPT, with Anthropic's Claude tested), echoing the open-core-under-proprietary-governance direction one level up. Net: real overlap with the agent-platform space, but the open-harness-specific claim is not what Apple shipped; scored 3.
